results.claim: The archive row X1 had called one-point Chowla (sum_{n<=x} lambda(n) = o(x)) OPEN; the document corrects this to: it is a theorem, equivalent to PNT (Mertens form M(y) = o(y)), via lambda = 1_squares * mu giving sum_{n<=x} lambda(n) = sum_{d<=sqrt(x)} M(x/d^2) = o(x). It also cites Tao arXiv:1605.04628 as the source and Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao arXiv:1509.01545 sec. 1 as an additional reference.
results.paper_quote: MRT 1509.01545 (read as HTML, v2), introduction after Conjecture 1.3 (Chowla): "For k = 1, this claim is equivalent to the prime number theorem, but for k > 1 Chowla's conjecture remains open." Tao 1605.04628 (read as HTML), introduction after Conjecture 1.1: "The k = 1 case of the Chowla conjecture is equivalent to the prime number theorem. The higher k cases are open" and "lambda(n) = sum_{d^2|n} mu(n/d^2)". No numbered theorem: both are unnumbered remarks in sec. 1.
results.doc_quote: "**false** -- it is **equivalent to PNT**, i.e. a **theorem**.  `lambda = 1_squares * mu`, so `Σ_{n≤x}lambda(n) = Σ_{d≤√x} M(x/d²) = o(x)` follows from `M(y) = o(y)`"; Status: "CITED (literature; `λ = 1_squares ∗ μ`, cited Tao [arXiv:1605.04628](...))".
results.notes: Both statements are unnumbered introduction remarks, so no numbering mismatch. Batch paper 1509.01545: v1 2015-09-04, v2 2015-09-23; only v2 exists and its HTML was read. The archive's own citation is Tao 1605.04628 (v1 only), read too; it gives the same sentence, so the attribution is faithful. k=1 Chowla with a_1=1,b_1=0 is exactly sum_{n<=x} lambda(n)=o(x); both papers treat k>1 (incl. sum lambda(n)lambda(n+2)) as open, as the document says. Paper prints the identity as lambda(n)=sum_{d^2|n} mu(n/d^2), equivalent to the document's convolution form. The witness (x=100,1000) is the document's own computation, not a citation; reproduced: L(100)=-2, L(1000)=-14, matching sum_d M(x/d^2).
